REUTERS: Mexico's Sheinbaum vows no protection for ex-Pemex chief after wife posts alleged abuse video
June 29, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Reuters ran it straight: Sheinbaum dropped a longtime ally — ex-Pemex head Víctor Rodríguez — the day his wife posted surveillance video of his abuse, quoting the president directly with no editorializing.

🇲🇽 A government that publicly cuts loose a powerful insider over domestic violence is the story; watch which US outlets reframe it as a "Morena scandal" instead.

• Sheinbaum: "Let the law be applied, we will not protect anyone."
• "There can be no violence against women."

NATIONAL REVIEW: Cracks Begin to Show in the Mexican Regime
June 30, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Joshua Treviño labels Mexico's elected government "the regime" and frames a sovereign decision — not handing citizens over on US indictments without extradition due process — as a "crisis."

🇲🇽 Declining to arrest people on a foreign government's say-so is not a "crack." It is how extradition law works in every sovereign state.

• "DOJ indictments of alleged Mexican narco-politicians from Morena — and the Mexican president's refusal to detain them — are leading to a crisis."

NYT: For These Teens in Mexico, Soccer Is Life. Now, the Cartels Want In.
June 29, 2026 | 🔴

📰 As Mexico co-hosts a World Cup that has gone off without a major incident, the NYT runs a feature on cartels extorting youth soccer leagues in Guanajuato — "If you play here, you must pay."

🇲🇽 Guanajuato is one of Mexico's most violent states; nationally homicides fell to ~44/day in May, below the US daily average — a trend the piece never mentions.

• cartel sign on the fields: "If you play here, you must pay"
• "13 players killed last year" in the Celaya metro zone; 14 so far this year
• "11 people gunned down after a game" in Salamanca in January

🇲🇽🏭 WOMEN DROVE MEXICO'S JOB GROWTH — AND STILL EARN 35% LESS

New labor data shows women's employment was effectively the only segment still growing into 2026, lifting the female workforce to 24.5 million. But the gap they're walking into is brutal: women average 23,714 pesos a quarter against men's 36,047 — roughly 35% less for the same economy. Sheinbaum's minimum-wage hikes are part of why more are entering at all: each increase measurably raises the odds a woman aged 25–54 joins the workforce.

🚨🇲🇽 TRUMP TAXED THE MIGRANTS — MEXICAN FAMILIES STILL HELD THE LINE

Washington's new 1% tax on non-citizen transfers, plus its migration crackdown, were built to choke the remittances that reach millions of Mexican households. In 2025 they forced the first annual drop in 11 years (-4.56%). Yet by the first four months of 2026 remittances were back up 2.6% year-on-year, at 19.68 billion dollars — sent, transfer by transfer, by the very people the empire spends every day trying to deport.

🔥🇲🇽 THE "IMSS COLLAPSE" THE PRESS PROMISED NEVER CAME — RESERVES NEAR 700 BILLION PESOS

After years of headlines forecasting the institute's bankruptcy, IMSS director Zoé Robledo laid out the numbers: financial reserves grew from 200 billion pesos in 2018 to nearly 700 billion, with projected financial sufficiency stretching to 2037. He called the "collapse" narrative "false or deliberately distorted information" — biased readings that quietly omit reserve growth, millions of new beneficiaries and rising worker-employer contributions.

🔥🇲🇽 "ROTOPAN": PAN LAWMAKERS SOLD WATER TANKS AND FRIDGES AS FAKE "SOCIAL PROGRAMS"

Morena filed a formal complaint accusing two Mexico City PAN deputies of running a pyramid scheme — using Congress logos and their own faces to push a 33-item catalog of tinacos, mattresses, TVs and washing machines at market price or higher, dressed up as a "subsidized social program" for the poor. The front association is run de facto by a former PAN mayor with five open criminal cases and a prior conviction for misappropriating public funds.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO IS AMONG THE 5 MOST-TRUSTED GOVERNMENTS IN THE ENTIRE OECD

While the foreign press sells a country in chaos, the OECD just placed Mexico among its five nations where most people trust their national government: 53% — a full 13 points above the OECD average of 40%, behind only Switzerland, Iceland, Norway and Luxembourg. Trust runs highest among those who lived through the neoliberal years — 60% among people over 50. Satisfaction with public services climbed from 67% to 72% in two years.

🚨🇲🇽 WASHINGTON CALLS MEXICO THE FENTANYL THREAT — ITS OWN DEA LET HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF PILLS FLOOD NEW MEXICO

For years Washington branded Mexican cartels "foreign terrorists" and leaned on Mexico's sovereignty in the name of fentanyl. Now New Mexico's own governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham, is moving to sue the DEA after agents deliberately let hundreds of thousands of fentanyl pills reach the streets to "build bigger cases" — a tactic one DEA official, David Howell, warned back in 2023 had "poisoned our community." The poison was flowing from inside the house all along.

🇲🇽🏭 $82.5 BILLION HEADED FOR MEXICAN DATA CENTERS: THE AI BUILDOUT LANDS SOUTH OF THE BORDER

Mexico is on track to capture $82.5 billion in data-center investment between 2026 and 2031, according to the Mexican Data Centers Association (MexDC) — projected to create 98,366 jobs during construction and 35,430 permanent operating positions. Querétaro alone holds 72% of the projects. The global AI boom needs power, land, and proximity to the US market, and capital is betting Mexico delivers all three (El Economista).
